title: Grandmommy’s Pound Cake
status: Complete editorial review; implemented and production verified

exactBefore.body:
## Chef's Note

Grandmommy’s pound cake has a rich, buttery crumb. The key is baking at 275°F for a full 90 minutes; this ensures the cake rises evenly without a tough outer crust, resulting in a dense, velvety texture that defines a true pound cake. Room temperature eggs are mandatory for a perfect emulsion.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Preheat oven to 275°F. Generously grease and flour a large Bundt pan or three 9x5 loaf pans.
2.  **Cream:** In a stand mixer, cream the butter and sugar on medium-high for 5-7 minutes until the mixture is pale, light, and doubled in volume.
3.  **Emulsify:** Add the eggs one at a time, beating for 30 seconds after each addition to ensure a stable structure.
4.  **Incorporate:** Reduce speed to low. Gradually add the pre-sifted flour in three parts, mixing until **just combined**.
5.  **Flavor:** Fold in the lemon, almond, and vanilla extracts by hand.
6.  **Bake:** Pour the thick batter into the prepared pan. Bake at 275°F for 1.5 hours (or at 300°F for 1 hour if using loaf pans) until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
7.  **Cool:** Let cool in the pan for 20 minutes before inverting onto a rack.

frontmatter.title: Grandmommy’s Pound Cake
frontmatter.cookTime: About 90 min for a large cake or 60 min for loaves; continue as needed
frontmatter.totalTime: About 3½–5 hr for a large cake or 2½–4 hr for loaves, including cooling
ingredients: 3/4 lb (3 sticks) unsalted butter, softened, not melted
baking pan spray, enough to grease all baking pans thoroughly
additional flour, enough to dust the greased pans; tap out the excess

steps.title: Choose the pans and oven route
steps.text: For one large cake, heat the oven to 275°F and use a roomy tube or Bundt pan. For the three-loaf route, heat the oven to 300°F and use three loaf pans for the original batch. Prepare every pan with {{ingredients}}, reaching corners and the center tube. Have an extra small cake pan ready if needed; the batter must not fill any pan more than two-thirds full.

steps.title: Cream the butter and sugar
steps.text: Beat {{ingredients}} at medium speed until noticeably paler and fluffy, scraping the sides and bottom of the bowl several times. Start checking after about 5 minutes; the texture matters more than a fixed volume increase. The butter should hold air rather than look oily or melted.

steps.title: Add the eggs gradually
steps.text: Add {{ingredients}} one at a time at medium-low speed, allowing each to incorporate before adding the next. Scrape the bowl between additions.

steps.title: Add the flour gently
steps.text: At low speed, mix in {{ingredients}} in several small additions. Stop as soon as the flour disappears, then check the bottom of the bowl for unmixed streaks.

steps.title: Add all three extracts
steps.text: Fold in {{ingredients}} by hand until evenly distributed.

steps.title: Fill with room to rise
steps.text: Scrape the batter into the prepared pan or divide it evenly among the loaf pans. Smooth the tops. Keep the batter level at or below two-thirds of each pan’s depth; if it exceeds that level, put the excess in the prepared extra pan rather than packing the main pan. A shallower loaf will bake more quickly than a deeper one.

steps.title: Bake by the center
steps.text: Bake a large cake at 275°F, using 90 minutes as the starting plan and beginning checks around 75 minutes. Bake the loaf route at 300°F, using 60 minutes as the starting plan and beginning checks around 45 minutes if the loaves are shallow. Keep the chosen temperature fixed as ingredient quantities change. Continue until the cake is set, the top springs back under a light touch, and a long tester or thin knife inserted into the thickest crumb in several places comes out without wet batter. Avoid the center tube, pan and surface cracks when checking. Tent loosely with foil if the top darkens before the middle finishes. Check individual loaves separately and remove each as it finishes. Start checking small overflow cakes earlier; their shallower depth can shorten the bake considerably.

steps.title: Cool before slicing or wrapping
steps.text: Rest in the pan on a rack for about 20 minutes. Loosen accessible edges, turn out carefully and cool completely on the rack before slicing or wrapping. If the cake is still fragile, let it settle a few minutes longer before turning it out.

learning.focus: Cream the butter, incorporate eggs gradually, and bake by the center.
learning.outcome: A fully baked, fine-crumbed cake that releases from the pan and slices cleanly after cooling.
before: Use the full listed unsalted butter, softened enough to indent but still holding its shape.
Let the eggs lose their refrigerator chill while preparing the pans, keeping total raw-egg counter time within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F.
Sift the all-purpose flour before measuring the listed cups; keep pan-dusting flour separate from the measured batter flour.
Choose one oven route: a large tube/Bundt cake at 275°F or three loaf pans for the original batch at 300°F. Leave room for the batter to rise, and prepare an extra pan if needed.

checkpoints.cue: The creamed butter and sugar are paler and fluffy, with no greasy pool.
checkpoints.why: Creaming supplies air to a formula with no added chemical leavener.

checkpoints.cue: The batter stays at or below two-thirds of the pan depth.
checkpoints.why: This general creamed-cake headroom leaves room for expansion; it does not make different pan geometries share one finish time.

checkpoints.cue: The middle is set, the top springs back and several thick-crumb checks show no wet batter.
checkpoints.why: A fixed clock or a probe in the surface crack can miss the interior.

troubleshooting.cause: The ingredients are too cold or eggs were incorporated too quickly.
troubleshooting.fix: Pause, scrape the bowl and mix gently; incorporate the remaining eggs gradually. Keep the ingredients at room temperature rather than adding cold eggs to softened fat.

troubleshooting.problem: The top darkens before the center bakes.
troubleshooting.cause: The batter is deep or the pan/oven browns the exterior quickly.
troubleshooting.fix: Tent loosely with foil and continue at the chosen temperature until the center checks are clear.

troubleshooting.cause: It is still fragile or the pan was insufficiently prepared.
troubleshooting.fix: Allow a little more pan rest, loosen accessible edges carefully and support the cake when turning it out. Grease every pan detail thoroughly next time.

learning.storage: Once completely cool, wrap airtight and keep in a cool, dry place for 1–2 days, or wrap slices well and freeze for longer storage. Thaw a wrapped portion at room temperature.
learning.timing: Plan about 20–30 minutes preparation. The large-cake route starts from 90 minutes baking at 275°F; the original three-loaf route starts from 60 minutes at 300°F. Add about 20 minutes of pan rest and roughly 1–2 hours for full rack cooling, continuing until completely cool. Pan depth and oven heat can extend the plan. When scaling, keep ingredient ratios together and choose enough pans with headroom; do not multiply temperatures, baking times or pan dimensions. For a fractional egg quantity, beat an egg and weigh out the required fraction rather than rounding the egg count.

exactAfter.body:
## Chef's Note

Lemon, almond and vanilla give this rich pound cake its familiar flavor. Cream the softened butter and sugar until light, then mix the flour gently. The slow large-cake bake and the warmer loaf bake are separate routes; let the center of each cake determine when it is ready.

## Directions

1. **Choose the pans and oven route:** For one large cake, heat the oven to 275°F and use a roomy tube or Bundt pan. For the three-loaf route, heat the oven to 300°F and use three loaf pans for the original batch. Prepare every pan with baking pan spray and additional flour, reaching corners and the center tube. Have an extra small cake pan ready if needed; the batter must not fill any pan more than two-thirds full.
2. **Cream the butter and sugar:** Beat unsalted butter and granulated sugar at medium speed until noticeably paler and fluffy, scraping the sides and bottom of the bowl several times. Start checking after about 5 minutes; the texture matters more than a fixed volume increase. The butter should hold air rather than look oily or melted.
3. **Add the eggs gradually:** Add large eggs one at a time at medium-low speed, allowing each to incorporate before adding the next. Scrape the bowl between additions.
4. **Add the flour gently:** At low speed, mix in all-purpose flour in several small additions. Stop as soon as the flour disappears, then check the bottom of the bowl for unmixed streaks.
5. **Add all three extracts:** Fold in lemon extract, almond extract, and vanilla extract by hand until evenly distributed.
6. **Fill with room to rise:** Scrape the batter into the prepared pan or divide it evenly among the loaf pans. Smooth the tops. Keep the batter level at or below two-thirds of each pan’s depth; if it exceeds that level, put the excess in the prepared extra pan rather than packing the main pan. A shallower loaf will bake more quickly than a deeper one.
7. **Bake by the center:** Bake a large cake at 275°F, using 90 minutes as the starting plan and beginning checks around 75 minutes. Bake the loaf route at 300°F, using 60 minutes as the starting plan and beginning checks around 45 minutes if the loaves are shallow. Keep the chosen temperature fixed as ingredient quantities change. Continue until the cake is set, the top springs back under a light touch, and a long tester or thin knife inserted into the thickest crumb in several places comes out without wet batter. Avoid the center tube, pan and surface cracks when checking. Tent loosely with foil if the top darkens before the middle finishes. Check individual loaves separately and remove each as it finishes. Start checking small overflow cakes earlier; their shallower depth can shorten the bake considerably.
8. **Cool before slicing or wrapping:** Rest in the pan on a rack for about 20 minutes. Loosen accessible edges, turn out carefully and cool completely on the rack before slicing or wrapping. If the cake is still fragile, let it settle a few minutes longer before turning it out.

sourceDifferences: All-butter purchased product total stays at the current ¾ lb/3 U.S. butter sticks. This replaces the original half-pound butter plus the selected contemporary 4-ounce margarine stick; it does not recover the original margarine label or promise identical crumb.

Six large eggs, all-purpose pre-sifted flour and modern extracts are retained current specifications. Native lemon and almond were called flavor, with vanilla unspecified; the three separate 1 tsp amounts are unchanged.
Current gradual eggs-then-flour all-butter mixing is deliberately retained; the native alternating flour/egg method remains in the exact private original.
Large tube/Bundt and source three-loaf baking routes remain distinct; fixed temperatures and center checks with headroom do not certify any exact pan capacity.
Pan grease/dusting allowances and fractional-egg scaling are explicit operating guidance, not recovered historical measurements.
